page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a KVM-virtualized GPU server configured with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor. It features 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.0 GB of RAM per core. The server integrates two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 96 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, meaning storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes.

Benchmark results place this configuration in the top tier (top 10%) for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench scores. It also achieves top-tier performance in Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput. However, its Passmark memory score falls into the average (middle 50%) category, representing a potential bottleneck for memory-latency-sensitive tasks.

The dual NVIDIA L40S GPUs deliver top-tier LLM inference speeds for small models, processing 5508.2 tokens per second. For medium models, prompt processing remains strong (top 25%) at 220.88 tokens per second. Performance scales down to average (middle 50%) for large models, where text generation reaches 4.14 tokens per second.

Given the high density of GPU and memory resources, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for parallel computing workloads, machine learning inference, and data science pipelines. The absence of local storage and average memory latency are balanced by exceptional raw compute power and high VRAM capacity, making it highly suitable for AI model serving, rendering, and high-throughput database operations.
